newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia prosecutor asks subversion case be heard.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia prosecutor asks subversion case be heard.

text.p: An Indonesian prosecutor said on Monday that the state's case against independent labour activist Mucthar Pakpahan for subversion and spreading hatred against the government was properly constituted and should be heard.
Prosecutor R. Moekiat told the South Jakarta State Court in an hour long response to Pakpahan's statement last week that the government had fulfilled all its legal requirements.
"The prosecutors request that the judge try this case because the indictment has been compiled in accordance with the law and it can become the basis for hearing this case," Moekiat said.
Pakpahan said last week he was being charged under laws that were out-of-date as they orginated in Dutch colonial times or before President Suharto's 30-year New Order government.
The 1963 Subversion law, implemented as an emergency presidential decree and never passed by parliament, carries a maximum penalty of death.
The three-judge panel will render its decision next Monday, often just formality in such political trials, whether to proceed with the case based upon the evidence presented to it.
Similar charges against nine members of the leftist People's Democratic Party (PRD) also continued to be heard in two Jakarta courts on Monday.

Meanwhile, in the East Java city of Surabaya, three labour activists who were PRD members rejected prosecutors indictments read last week accusing them of subversion and spreading hatred against the government.

"Eighty percent of the prosecutor's indictment is trying our thoughts. Nobody may be threatened with the death sentence because of their thoughts," one of the three Surabaya defendants, Dita Indah Sari, told the Surabaya State Court.

Most of the PRD members were arrested in a crackdown after the July 27 riots in Jakarta, regarded as the worst in more than 20 years, in which at least five people died. However, none of their indictments directly links them to those events.

All the PRD members are being tried for their membership of the unrecognised group that does not use the state ideology as its basis and among other things, calls for major changes in the role of the Indonesian military in the nation's political life.
Pakpahan, who is not a PRD member, is being tried separately for statements he made in a book, speeches, news releases and a music cassette of workers songs between mid-1995 and July this year.
